donnees.titre: Iris melanoma with seeding along a glaucoma drainage device: A case report.
donnees.revue: American journal of ophthalmology case reports
donnees.resume:
INTRODUCTION: Iris melanoma represents approximately 4% of uveal melanomas, and extraocular seeding is rare. Tumor spread along a glaucoma drainage device is exceptionally uncommon and may mimic inflammatory or vascular processes, leading to delayed diagnosis.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 78-year-old male with advanced glaucoma and prior glaucoma drainage devices developed a progressively enlarging, vascular, initially amelanotic iris lesion with rising intraocular pressure. Over several months, the lesion became increasingly pigmented with new subconjunctival changes. Early fine-needle aspiration was limited by low cellularity and lack of ocular pathology review, yielding a small nonspecific lymphoid population insufficient for diagnosis. As clinical progression continued, conjunctival biopsies performed using a no-touch technique confirmed malignant melanoma. Intraoperative findings demonstrated tumor extension from the iris into the subconjunctival space along a prior glaucoma drainage tract, prompting orbital exenteration. The patient was advised to complete adjuvant radiation therapy, but was subsequently lost to follow-up. He later re-established care with outside oncology providers, where he was diagnosed with metastatic parotid involvement and began systemic immunotherapy.
CONCLUSION: This case illustrates a rare presentation of iris melanoma with extraocular seeding through a glaucoma drainage device. Recognition of vascular or amelanotic iris lesions, attention to rising intraocular pressure, and timely no-touch biopsy are critical. Long-term multidisciplinary surveillance remains essential due to metastatic potential.
